trait.name: Pack Tactics
entries: The tunneler has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the tunneller's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn't {@condition incapacitated}.

trait.name: Tunneller
entries: The tunneller can burrow through solid rock at half its burrowing speed and can leave a 5-foot-diameter tunnel in its wake

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) piercing damage plus 3 ({@damage 1d6}) cold damage.

action.name: Ice Breath {@recharge 6}
entries: The tunneller exhales icy shards in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a {@dc 12} Dexterity saving throw, taking 7 ({@damage 2d6}) piercing damage and 7 ({@damage 2d6}) cold damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

While adults of the species can grow to gargantuan sizes, this juvenile is roughly the size of a horse. Its scaly hide is pale white, and sprouting from its back are several blue crystals of ice. Frost Tunnellers are lone creatures, and thus the juveniles are often found without parental supervision. Instead, they often take up the position of pack leader, lording over other, smaller creatures, using their tunnelling abilities to create an underground nest for themselves and their pack.

trait.name: Tunneler
entries: The aurumvorax can burrow through solid rock and metal at half its burrowing speed and leaves a 5-foot-diameter tunnel in its wake.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The aurumvorax makes one Bite attack and two Claw attacks.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 4} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d8 + 2}) piercing damage. If the target is a creature wearing armor of any type, the aurumvorax regains 4 ({@dice 1d6 + 1}) hit points.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d6 + 2}) slashing damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it is {@condition grappled} (escape {@dc 12}). Until this grapple ends, the aurumvorax can't use its Claw attack on another target, and when it moves, it can drag the {@condition grappled} creature with it, without the aurumvorax's speed being halved.

Early in life, aurumvoraxes cooperate with siblings and their den leader parents, digging tunnels in search of metal and other burrowing prey. As they grow to adulthood, aurumvoraxes hunt on their own, carving out territories they viciously defend.

entries.name: Aurumvorax
entries: An aurumvorax is an eight-legged, badger-like hunter. These aggressive omnivores attack any prey they think they can best, ambushing even creatures double their size. They supplement their diets with metal, whether it's worked or ore, and they have a particular taste for gold. This diet lends aurumvorax fur its golden sheen.

Alone or in small groups, aurumvoraxes dig deep in search of precious metals. Such exploration often leads them into conflict with subterranean settlements. As defenders of such communities often wear metal armor, aurumvoraxes prioritize attacking armored foes—whether that armor is metal or not.

spellcasting.name: Mutated Spellcasting
headerEntries: Due to the confluence of necromantic magic and exposure to the waters of an Emergence Pool, Tunneler has gained the ability to channel magic. His spellcasting modifier is Wisdom (spell save {@dc 11}) and he can innately cast the following spells, requiring no components:

trait.name: Assassinate
entries: During its first turn, the assassin has advantage on attack rolls against any creature that hasn't taken a turn. Any hit the assassin scores against a {@status surprised} creature is a critical hit.

trait.name: Sneak Attack
entries: Once per turn, the assassin deals an extra 10 ({@damage 3d6}) damage when it hits a target with a weapon attack and has advantage on the attack roll, or when the target is within 5 feet of an ally of the assassin that isn't {@condition incapacitated} and the assassin doesn't have disadvantage on the attack roll.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The assassin makes two dagger attacks.

action.name: Dagger
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d4 + 3}) piercing damage plus 7 ({@damage 2d6}) poison damage, and the target can't take reactions until the start of their next turn.

bonus.name: Cunning Action
entries: The assassin takes the Dash, Disengage, or Hide action.

bonus.name: Smoke Bomb (2/Day)
entries: The assassin deploys a small smoke bomb, creating a 5-foot-radius sphere of smoke centred on a point within 10 feet. The area of this smoke cloud is {@quickref Vision and Light|PHB|2||heavily obscured}. The smoke dissipates at the start of the assassin's next turn.

Trained from birth, these Quorum agents deal in death, rather than diplomacy. Whenever the Quorum has a problem that cannot be solved any other way, they dispatch one of these assassins, with strict instructions to escape custody if caught and slay those responsible for their capture. However, if attempting to fulfil this goal means certain death, they will flee, and live to serve the Quorum another day.

trait.name: Paint Form
entries: The globlin can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing. It can also merge itself with any painted surface, becoming indistinguishable from the surface while it remains motionless.

trait.name: Death Burst
entries: When the globlin dies, it explodes in a burst of colourful paint. Each creature within 15 feet of it must then succeed on a {@dc 13} Dexterity saving throw or be {@condition blinded} until the end of its next turn. All paint globlins are immune to the death bursts of each other.

action.name: Glob Lob
entries: The paint globlin throws a handful of paint at a creature it can see within 90 feet. That creature must succeed on a {@dc 13} Dexterity saving throw or be {@condition blinded} for one minute, or until it or another creature uses an action to clear the paint from its eyes.

action.name: Clobber
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 3} to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 1}) bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Paint Roller
entries: The globlin moves up to its speed in a straight line without provoking opportunity attacks. If this movement takes the globlin through the space of a Medium or smaller creature, that creature must succeed on a {@dc 13} Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 1d6 + 3} bludgeoning damage and fall {@condition prone}. The globlin cannot stop in another creature's space.

Paint globlins are created when an elemental spirit of earth is summoned and tied to the minerals in paint. They will generally obey orders given by their summoner, especially if those orders involve causing mischief.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 3} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}14 ({@damage 4d6}) piercing damage.

action.name: Bandages
entries: The skullholder uses a random bandage effect, choosing a target that it can see within 40 feet of it.

items.name: 1. Dreadful Bandage
items.entry: The targeted creature must succeed on a {@dc 15} Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition frightened} for 1 minute. If the target fails the saving throw by 5 or more, it is also {@condition paralyzed} while it is {@condition frightened} this way. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

items.name: 2. Corrupting Bandage
items.entry: The target must succeed on a {@dc 15} Charisma saving throw, or it can't take reactions until the end of its next turn. On its turn, the target can't move, and it uses its action to make a melee or ranged attack against a randomly determined target within range. If the target can't attack, it does nothing on its turn.

items.name: 3. Wrapping Bandage
entries: If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a {@dc 15} Strength saving throw or the skullholder moves it up to 30 feet in any direction. It is {@condition restrained} by the grip of the skullholder's bandages until the start of the skullholder's next turn or until the skullholder is {@condition incapacitated}.

If the target is an object weighing 300 pounds or less that isn't being worn or carried, it is moved up to 30 feet in any direction. The skullholder can also exert fine control on objects with this bandage effect, such as manipulating a simple tool or opening a door or a container.

items.name: 4. Rotting Bandage
entries: If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw or take 36 ({@damage 8d8}) necrotic damage, and its hit point maximum decreases by half that amount. On a success, the creature takes half damage and its hit point maximum does not decrease.

If the target is a Large or smaller nonmagical object made of organic material such as wood, it rots away without a saving throw. If the target is a Huge or larger nonmagical object made of organic material, this bandage effect rots a 10-foot cube of it.

Created as part of an experiment to perfect the mummified form, this creature is formed from a mummified head wrapped in bandages. These bandages float freely and, like a beholder's eye stalks, are able to create myriad effects.
All skullholders long to be freed from the laboratories they were created in, and will use whatever means at their disposal to convince any intruders to take them with them.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The skullholder has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Undead Nature
entries: The skullholder doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (1/Day)
entries: If the skullholder fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

reaction.name: Bandage Absorption {@recharge 5}
entries: As a reaction to taking damage, the skullholder can roll {@dice 4d6} and reduce the damage taken by that amount.

legendary.name: Bandages
entries: The skullholder uses one random bandage effect.

trait.name: Shadow Stealth
entries: While in dim light or darkness, the shadow can take the {@action Hide} action as a bonus action. Its stealth bonus is also improved to +8.

trait.name: Light Weakness
entries: While in bright light, the shadow has disadvantage on attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws.

trait.name: Incorporeal Movement
entries: The shadow (copy) can move through other creatures and objects as if they were {@quickref difficult terrain||3}. It takes 5 ({@damage 1d10}) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

action.name: Shade Touch
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 6} to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. {@h}9 ({@damage 1d8 + 4}) necrotic damage.
Grave Shades are undead created when a humanoid's life force is drained from them.

monster.name: Undercover Undead
languages: the languages it knew in life

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The undead casts one of the following spells, using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 13}):

trait.name: Ring of Life's Guise
entries: While wearing this ring, the undead that is attuned to it appears as it did in life. This illusion is dispelled if the undead casts a spell that requires {@status concentration}.

trait.name: Unusual Nature
entries: The undead doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The undead makes two Life Drain or Grave Bolt attacks.

action.name: Life Drain
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 4} to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d6 + 3}) necrotic damage. The target must succeed on a {@dc 13} Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the target takes an additional 5 ({@damage 1d4 + 3}) necrotic damage, and the undead regains hit points equal to half the total damage dealt. On a success, the target does not take the additional damage, and the undead does not regain hit points.

action.name: Grave Blast
entries: {@atk rs} {@hit 5} to hit, range 120 ft., one target. {@h}9 ({@damage 1d10 + 3}) necrotic damage. The target must succeed on a {@dc 13} Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the target's hit point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the damage taken. This reduction lasts until the target finishes a long rest. the target dies if its hit point maximum is reduced to 0.
If this attack kills a Humanoid, a {@creature grave shade|TheWheel} immediately appears in the target's space.

Often used as undercover agents by the Cult of Sokar, these undead were once living, willing members of the cult who chose to become undead to further their master's cause. They gain magical abilities from their master, much as a Warlock might from their patron. They can be found all across the Wheel, disguised as simple travellers, adventurers, or even important members of a community.
